content: 1. Lansoprazole can increase the levels or effects of clobazam by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction may require dosage adjustments, as CYP2C19 inhibitors can lead to increased exposure to N-desmethylclobazam, the active metabolite of clobazam. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Lansoprazole reduces the effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration of lansoprazole with clopidogrel in healthy subjects who are extensive metabolizers of CYP2C19 resulted in a 14% reduction in the mean AUC of clopidogrel’s active metabolite. This may reduce clopidogrel’s efficacy, as its antiplatelet activity depends entirely on its active metabolite. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Lansoprazole decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces the solubility and bioavailability of crizotinib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended, although no formal studies have been conducted. 6. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 8. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam (both buccal and intranasal forms) by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may slow diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Lansoprazole increases the toxicity of digoxin due to prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), which may cause hypomagnesemia and increase the risk of digoxin toxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Encorafenib affects lansoprazole by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Serum potassium should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Lansoprazole decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. Co-administration with PPIs should be avoided if possible. If PPI treatment is required, separate gefitinib and PPI doses by 12 hours. 21. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant administration may increase tacrolimus whole blood concentrations, particularly in intermediate or poor metabolizers of CYP2C19. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies to mycophenolate mofetil but is less significant for enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of methylphenidate by altering its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of methotrexate by decreasing renal clearance, which increases the risk of toxicity, particularly at higher doses. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of iron dextran complex, iron sucrose, and polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of lomitapide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 32. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of lenacapavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of nefazodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of St. John’s Wort by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur. 37. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, tazemetostat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tecovirimat by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. Conversely, tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
